newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: High-income earners benefit from savings plan - Oppn.
newsitem.headline: High-income earners benefit from savings plan - Oppn.

text.p: The Labor Opposition said on Wednesday the government's savings rebate plan would not benefit the average Australian and had been set up to boost the ruling Liberal-National coalition's election prospects in 1999.
Opposition Leader Kim Beazley said he had calculated (see table below) that high income earners would be the only beneficiaries of the plan to introduce a 15 percent rebate on savings income.
"What the average Australian has lost on average weekly earnings is A$100,000 on retirement," Beazley told reporters.

"What (Treasurer) Mr (Peter) Costello has done is to take A$3.5 billion off the average Australian in this budget in his savings task and to hand himself A$1 billion for an election slush fund in two years from now."

In its 1997/98 budget announced on Tuesday evening, the government said it would replace a tax promised, but never delivered by the former Labor government, with its own 15 percent rebate on savings income.
